tone_patterns: Formal, institutional tone that frames topics as organisational priorities and capabilities
Action-oriented phrasing that links initiatives to intended outcomes (e.g., foster, enhance, reduce, promote)
Risk-aware language that describes consequences of inadequate management before presenting mitigations
Balanced emphasis on people, governance, and operational resilience within a strategy narrative
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a cross-reference sentence directing readers to a separate report for deeper detail
Uses a short lead-in paragraph stating the strategic intent, followed by bullet lists of initiatives
Alternates between narrative explanation and structured lists to improve scanability
Introduces a subtopic with a descriptive heading, then provides context, then enumerates actions/controls
Includes a compact ‘activities conducted’ list where each item is a label followed by a brief description
Uses cause–effect paragraphs: describes risk exposure, then explains governance/controls that mitigate it
heading_patterns: Section-level header repeated in page footer/header area (e.g., ‘Strategy’) for navigation
Subheadings use title case and are descriptive (e.g., topic + management focus)
Occasional long subheading that combines assessment/management framing with scope qualifier (e.g., internal operations)
Figure titles follow a consistent pattern: ‘Figure X: [descriptive title]’ placed immediately above the visual
table_patterns: No tables present in this excerpt; list structures are used in place of tabular presentation
Where multiple initiatives are grouped, the layout mimics a table via aligned labels and short descriptions
figure_or_diagram_patterns: A numbered figure is used to summarise a concept as ‘pillars’ or thematic groupings
Figure content appears as a cluster of short labels (pillar names) rather than long explanatory text
Figure is introduced by a caption and then supported by surrounding narrative and bullets
Figure acts as a visual index to subsequent detailed items (labels echoed in later text)
pdf_layout_patterns: Two-page spread feel with consistent page numbering and repeated section identifier at the bottom
Figure placed near the top portion of the page, followed by bullets and narrative blocks
Use of indentation and bullet hierarchy (primary bullets with nested sub-bullets) to show structure
Line breaks and short paragraphs used to fit narrow column widths typical of PDF report layouts
Footer includes report title and section name for wayfinding; page number aligned consistently
Occasional standalone lines (e.g., report name references) used as navigational or contextual markers
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses ‘approach’ framing to describe management methods (e.g., ‘approach includes the following’)
Employs ‘committed to’ and ‘dedicated to’ constructions to express policy-level intent without over-detailing
References recognised frameworks/standards as alignment statements, followed by a list of controls
Describes governance as enabling accountability, scrutiny, and approvals across departments
Risk disclosure pattern: identifies risk area, outlines potential impacts, then lists mitigation measures
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented as examples of programmes and controls rather than extensive quantitative detail
When metrics are included, they are embedded within narrative or bullet items as outcome indicators
Uses ‘includes’ lists to evidence comprehensiveness (audits, training, compliance, monitoring)
Mentions internal monitoring and reporting practices as proof of ongoing oversight
section_specific_observations: Strategy content blends human capital topics with operational risk management and governance/ethics
The excerpt uses a ‘pillar’ visual to organise workforce themes, then expands via initiative lists
Digital/data risk is treated as an operational sustainability-related risk with governance and control responses
Cross-referencing to other publications is used to keep the strategy section concise while signalling depth elsewhere
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organisation name, report titles, or branded programme names
Any specific percentages, headcounts, dates, or time-bound performance statements
Any country-specific references or alignment claims tied to a particular national vision
Any named external standards or certifications presented as factual compliance for the reference entity
Any specific risk statements implying actual incidents, deficiencies, or regulatory positions
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: References to a separate ESG report and a momentum report by name
Specific workforce size, engagement score, turnover rate, and gender representation figures
Specific year references and ‘as at’ date references
Named cybersecurity and information security frameworks/standards and specific certification references
Mentions of particular governance artefacts (e.g., code of conduct topics) as applied to the reference entity
Geography-specific wording and references to a national vision
